questions: What is the exact timeline: how many days does app store review typically take for each platform, and what is the realistic latest submission date that still guarantees approval and availability before the sale starts?
What share of the 2 million users will actually have the updated app installed by the time the push notification goes out, and how many will still be on the old checkout during the sale?

How well does the beta population represent the full user base (device types, OS versions, regions, payment methods, new vs. returning customers), and is an 8% conversion lift likely to hold at sale-week traffic?
Has the new checkout been load-tested at the peak concurrency expected when 2 million users are notified at once, including payment provider, inventory, and backend rate limits?

Beyond crash rates, what other failure modes could the beta have missed, such as payment failures, abandoned carts due to bugs, promo-code or discount handling, tax calculation, or accessibility issues?

If a serious checkout problem appears during the sale, what is the fastest way to mitigate it (server-side feature flag, kill switch, staged rollout, halting the release), and how long would a full rollback via a new app update actually take?
Can the new checkout be released behind a remotely controlled flag or phased rollout so that exposure is limited and can be turned off without a new app update?
What is the expected revenue upside of the 8% lift during the sale week compared with the potential loss from an outage or degraded checkout, and how likely is each scenario?
Does the new checkout work correctly with sale-specific mechanics (discount codes, bundles, flash pricing, gift cards, stock limits), and have those flows been tested end to end?

Do customer support, engineering on-call, and monitoring and alerting have the capacity and readiness to detect and respond to checkout issues in real time during the first hours of the sale, and is there a code freeze or buffer period after shipping?
